Watch what the dummy does after the initial stumble as well as how it reacts on contact.

paragraphs: When comparing weapons, keep what you saw the dummy do separate from what the scan shows. If an arm stops moving normally, for example, that tells you where to look in the X-ray view. Wait until you see a break before counting it as one in your comparison.

Body Scan is for inspection: opening the X-ray view doesn’t cause a break or repair one. For a closer look at the feature and how injuries affect dummy movement, see the Hyper Realistic Ragdoll Body Scan Guide.

sections.intro: If you want to bring a dummy back, look for a Medkit or Defibrillator rather than switching to another weapon. Either tool is an option for recovery; you don’t need to look for both.
paragraphs: The game’s Roblox listing doesn’t distinguish between the two tools’ recovery effects. If only one is available in your session, start with that one. If the game shows a prompt for the tool you choose, follow it rather than assuming the item works a certain way because of its name.

faq.question: Where can you find the weapons list in Hyper Realistic Ragdoll?
faq.answer: Look for Weapons and Tools in the description of Emo Playworks' Roblox experience. That section is useful for checking the spelling of an item such as Void Gun or Flamethrower. It names featured weapons rather than presenting a complete inventory, so an item missing from that list is not necessarily absent from the game.

faq.question: How do you unlock weapons in Hyper Realistic Ragdoll?
faq.answer: Playing the experience unlocks more weapons, but the Roblox description does not pair each named weapon with a specific milestone. If an item is still locked, follow any requirement the game shows for that item. Its appearance in the description does not mean it is available when you start.

faq.question: How do weapons interact with ragdoll physics?
faq.answer: A dummy can react differently depending on which body part is affected. For example, a broken arm can hang limp without producing the same movement change as a leg injury. When comparing two items, look at what the dummy can still do afterward rather than treating every visible reaction as the same result.

sections.intro: Pick a dummy you can see clearly and watch it for a moment before you grab it. Notice whether it’s standing still or already moving, and pay attention to where its arms and legs are. In Hyper Realistic Ragdoll, each body part can respond independently, so a change in one limb can tell you more than the dummy’s overall movement.
paragraphs: Use what you saw to choose your next test. If you lost track of the arms during the swing, repeat the swing and watch just one arm. If you suspect a break, use Body Scan to check the bone in the in-game X-ray.

If you'd rather watch an encounter, look for the zombies that rise from the graveyard. Give them a visit of their own so you can focus on what they do without splitting your attention between the zombies and a disaster.

hero.heading: Hyper Realistic Ragdoll Body Scan Guide
hero.lead: Hyper Realistic Ragdoll Body Scan gives you an X-ray view of a dummy’s broken bones. A dummy’s movement gives you a separate clue about which body part reacted. In the game, a dummy can limp after a hit to the leg and crawl after a leg breaks, while a broken arm hangs slack. If you’re looking for the scan input, use any in-game prompt shown for your device. The table pairs body parts with their reactions, and the steps show how to compare what you see in motion with what appears on the scan.

sections.heading: Body Scan Shows Broken Bones in X-Ray
sections.intro: Use Body Scan to inspect a dummy’s bones in an X-ray view. The feature is useful when you want to check for a visible break rather than infer an injury from movement alone. To read the image, choose the body area you want to examine, open the scan, and look for a break shown in that area. For example, if you want to check an arm, focus on the arm in the X-ray and see whether a break is visible. Keep this observation separate from what the dummy does afterward: this section is about reading the scan, while the reaction table explains movement clues.
paragraphs: The scan description confirms that Body Scan shows broken bones, but it does not describe color coding, labels, or a separate indicator for other injury types. Use the visible X-ray as your check for a break, and avoid treating an unclear image as confirmation. Once you have inspected the relevant area, compare the result with the dummy’s reaction using the table below.

sections.intro: In Hyper Realistic Ragdoll, each part of a Roblox dummy reacts independently. Punches, shots, and blasts can all change how a dummy moves, but the reaction depends on the area affected and what happened to it. For a leg, the key distinction is whether the dummy is still taking steps or has switched to crawling.
paragraphs: When the reaction is harder to place, look at how much of the dummy’s movement changed. A slack arm is a clue about one limb, while fainting is a whole-dummy response. Use those differences to decide which body area to check, not as proof of a fracture. A head hit that makes a dummy faint, for example, doesn’t by itself tell you that a bone broke.

paragraphs: If you need mappings for other actions, see the Hyper Realistic Ragdoll controls guide when it is available. Return to the same dummy after scanning if you want to compare the X-ray with its visible reaction.

sections.heading: Watch the Same Dummy Before and After the Scan
sections.intro: Pick one dummy and note where it starts relative to a nearby landmark, such as a wall. Write down its first reaction before opening Body Scan. After checking the X-ray, find that same dummy again, even if it has moved from its starting spot. If you lose track of it in a group, start a fresh observation rather than using another dummy for the last step.
paragraphs: Keep the scan result separate from what the dummy does afterward. If it gets back up or fights back by the time you return, record that as a later action, not as a replacement for what you saw first. Getting up alone doesn’t tell you whether the break you saw is still visible on the scan. If you use a Medkit or Defibrillator to bring the dummy back, note that between observations so you don’t confuse it with the dummy getting up on its own.
Here’s a sample note you can adapt to what you see:
bullets: First reaction: The dummy started beside a wall and stumbled.
Scan result: I saw a break in the arm.
After the scan: The same dummy was back on its feet when I returned.

faq.question: Does Body Scan show every kind of limb damage?
faq.answer: The X-ray is for looking at broken bones. If you’re trying to understand a change in movement, keep a separate note of what the dummy did. Limping describes how it moved during that moment, while a visible break tells you what appeared in the bone view.

faq.question: Which key activates Body Scan?
faq.answer: The Roblox description explains the X-ray feature without naming an activation key. If a Body Scan prompt appears during play, follow the input it displays. When sharing that input with another player, include your device so they can compare it with the controls on their own screen.

faq.question: Does a dummy fainting tell me what will appear on Body Scan?
faq.answer: Fainting is the dummy’s listed reaction to a head hit. To tell someone what happened, describe the fainting as the reaction you saw, then report any visible break from the X-ray as a separate observation. That gives them both the movement cue and the finding from the scan.

sections.intro: Both the Medkit and the Defibrillator can revive dummies in Hyper Realistic Ragdoll. Try one tool at a time on a dummy that's still down. Dummies can also get up on their own, so the key detail is whether the dummy starts to rise before or after you use the tool.

faq.question: Can a dummy get back up on its own?
faq.answer: Dummies can get back up as part of their normal behavior. If you want to see whether that happens, pause before using a recovery item and watch the same dummy. If it stands while you're waiting, you can observe that recovery without using an equipment control.

hero.heading: Hyper Realistic Ragdoll Bat Guide

sections.heading: Find the Bat by Its In-Game Name
sections.intro: Check the creator credit before opening a search result on Roblox. The original Hyper Realistic Ragdoll is by Emo Playworks. A similar title or thumbnail can lead to a different experience with different equipment, so use the creator name to make sure you’re checking the right game.

sections.heading: Check the Bat’s Unlock Requirement

If the Bat is locked and shows a condition, follow the wording on the entry. If it names a particular task or prerequisite, use that wording to decide what to do next.
If the Bat is locked and gives no condition, leave the requirement open. A lock by itself gives you no reason to chase a specific knockout total or spend currency.
If you see no Bat entry, continue with equipment you can select. The absence of an entry in the view you checked leaves its availability open.

sections.heading: Check Selection, Equip Status, and Input
sections.intro: If you can select the Bat, check what changes after you do. If the selection opens item details, read any instruction there before returning to the play area. If you see a separate equip action, use it and look for a sign that the selection carried over, such as the Bat appearing in your character’s hands. A highlighted entry may only show which item you’re viewing.
paragraphs: Use the action shown for the equipped item on your current device, if one appears. If you’re following a video, check which device the player is using before copying the input. A button in a recording of a touch interface gives you little guidance about which key to press on a keyboard. The [controls guide](/controls) covers general game inputs.

If nothing happens when you try the action, go back to the last step you completed. Check equip status first if you only saw the item’s details. If you can see the Bat equipped, focus on the action prompt and try one input at a time so you can tell which one the game responds to.

If it stumbles and then stands, you’ve seen a stumble followed by recovery. If a second effect interrupts the interaction, start a fresh attempt when you can watch the dummy without interference.

If the dummy already had a broken bone before the attempt, carry that detail forward when you read the second scan. This is especially useful when the dummy has already been involved in other interactions. The scan can tell you about the dummy’s condition, while the item entry is where you’d look for any unlock instruction.

faq.answer: Ask your friend to open the item entry in the same Roblox experience and compare what appears on both screens. If your screen gives you a prerequisite, follow its wording. A friend’s equipped Bat shows what they can use and may give you an item name to search for.
